defects: Pairs 1/6 s apart are almost identical. Within each shot, motion is a slow, constant drift of the light and dust motes, with no visible acceleration or settle, so it reads as linear.
The window-grid shot has its wordmark 'Lumen' sitting on top of the lit apertures. The title and the grid compete, and the lower-left windows are cut off behind the type.
The water-caustic panel shows a faint rectilinear tile seam or grid behind the pattern at 1:1, which reads as a texture repeat or compositing artefact.
In the caustic shot the small credit lines ('Anna Voss — projection…') are low-contrast tan over a busy, moving caustic. They are close to illegible and slightly soft at 100%.

The end card tiles the word as 'LUMENLUMEN' with the letters cropped at the frame edge and almost no gap at the join. 'lumen.fest' is caught mid-reveal ('lumen.fes'), so the type-on is a plain linear wipe.
Frame 1 is a single vertical beam on near-black with nothing else in frame: dead air that won't hold as a poster.
The caustic shot breaks the raking-beam-and-dust-mote language. Its lighting is flat and its colour is a muddy olive-brown that doesn't match the warm sodium beams elsewhere.
gaps: Choreography: nothing is driven by a force. The beam, grid and wordmark each just drift or wipe, with no light sweep that actually reveals the type on cue, no overshoot or settle, and no handoff where one shot's light becomes the next shot's aperture. The 'light through letterforms' idea is stated, but the film never stages it as an event.

Arc and pacing: three loosely related shots with a flat energy curve, a near-static opening beam and no peak at 60-80%. The caustic programme card is a different visual world dropped into the middle rather than a build toward the L/LUMEN payoff.

Finish: the light needs real volumetric depth (layered haze, beam falloff, bloom on the lit type edges) and the caustic plate needs to be seamless. Hierarchy also needs work: tiny tan captions over busy texture and a wordmark that collides with the grid fall short of the typographic precision top studios hold.
